summary: Backend-only in-process tests of MOD fault emails (Pulse desk escalation + supplier). 17/17 pytest pass. Verified: Point of contact = reporter name/email/phone + site name + structured address (line1..country) + legacy comma 'address' fallback + BFPO; JOB/SITE/MACHINE/FAULT sections one item per row in the required order (optional Type/Location/Steps/Photos only when present); serial in table, header line ('Rower · S/N x'), Sicon summary and both subjects (regex-matched '[MOD URGENT] ref — site — machine — S/N x' and '[Fault Log] ... — S/N x'); no '()' output, no S/N text when serial missing; safe_in_service=no -> 'Usable?: No — not safe to use (taken out of service)' even with usable=yes, and stored issue usable='no'; model equal to serial prefix -> 'Not on file'; Sicon block has all Label: value lines + Contact name/email/phone; site-typed text HTML-escaped (script/img/i/u tags); utils.email header with no logo shows site name only (no 38px chip); send_email for a MOD org with category='mod' (resend.Emails.send mocked) produced html/subject/from/reply_to with zero 'pulsefitness.ai' / 'Pulse Fitness AI'; mod_fault_submit called in-process with send_email mocked (result_out message_id='TEST_mid') -> Pulse + supplier notified_recipients both delivered=True and message_id='TEST_mid'. No real email sent (resend guard confirmed not hit). All TEST_ data cleaned up by id (verified 0 leftovers).

minor.issue: Dead code: `steps_row` is still built (with UNESCAPED steps_taken) in both functions but never used. Remove to avoid someone re-inserting it unescaped.

Header 'S/N' line uses eq.serial_number only, while the table falls back to doc.serial_number. If equipment has no serial but the issue does, table shows it but header/subject don't (minor inconsistency).
'N attached (shown below)' counts attachment_urls even when get_object fails and _inline_attachment_block renders nothing -> says 'shown below' with no photos shown.

Delivery stamp retries only 10x0.5s waiting for notified_recipients to be written; that write happens after create_supplier_case + make_fault_booking for every supplier. If those are slow (>5s) the Pulse entry's delivered/message_id stamp is silently lost. Consider writing notified_recipients before spawning the send tasks.
Reporter confirmation email still interpolates site/equipment/reporter text without _e() escaping (not in scope of this change but same untrusted input).
